text:
alex: Quick heads-up — seeing latency regressions on FP8+INT8 mixed runs when continuous-batcher is enabled. Root cause looks like slab/stride mismatch in KV cache slice selection.

maria: How bad? numbers?

alex: From local microbench: streaming median token latency went from 22ms -> 47ms on t4p2 with batcher=continuous, quant profile=fp8-int8-hybrid. Throughput stable but tail up.

jit: Any kernel fallback logs? could be picking dense GEMM for odd shape.

alex: yes, dispatch shows we pick kernel: kernel_v2_dense_int8_stride=128 for shapes that used to hit kernel_packed_fp8_stride=160. Reason: our slab-slicer rounds down to 128 when kv_len%64 !=0 — triggers different kernel family.

sam: That rounding sounds familiar — we added that heuristic for memory alignment. can you paste the dispatch trace?

alex: (paste)
```
[DISPATCH] seq_len=1024, kv_slots=17, kv_stride=1536
selector: slab_slicer -> slab_stride=128
selected_kernel: dense_int8_v2
fallback: none
perf_est: 1.8x slower
```

maria: Wait kv_slots=17? that's coming from batch packing when continuous batching merges short contexts. So uneven kv_slots -> stride mismatch.

irene: Is calibration changing weight packing sizes? FP8 calibration introduced block reshuffle for rounding — maybe changed kernel compatibility table.

alex: Bingo. After FP8 calibration we also enable 128-block packing for some layers (saves memory) but our kernel table expects 160-block for fp8-packed kernels. So we lose fp8-optimized kernel.

jit: Two fixes: 1) extend kernel selector to accept compatible block sizes (allow 128->160 mapping), 2) tweak slab_slicer to prefer packing that preserves kernel family when possible.

maria: Any regressions in quality from mapping 128->160? Calibration had per-channel scales, clipping differs but runtime uses same dequant; need check evals.

alex: Quick eval on evalset-A: perplexity change: +0.12% (negligible). Latency improvement: median token latency back to 24ms with patch.

perf-bot: CI perf run #2468: before patch median=46.9ms, after=23.7ms, p95 from 89ms -> 42ms, throughput +3%

sam: Are we sure this won't oscillate under different batch distributions? continuous-batcher produces many odd kv_slots.

jit: Add a fallback kernel scoring metric that factors stride mismatch cost; and emit telemetry when selector downgrades kernel family.

alex: I'll land a small change: selector mapping + telemetry. Also will add a sampler in continuous-batcher to prefer pack-aligned grouping when slack < 8 tokens.

irene: Add a note in release notes: FP8 calibration may change packing -> impacts kernel selection; we auto-fix but customer-facing note useful.

maria: Great. Alex, open PR and attach perf logs.

alex: PR: https://git.redwood/infra/PR/4567 — includes dispatch unit tests + perf run logs. Will watch canary.

sam: Thanks. If we see other regressions, tag me and I'll help rollback scheduler config.

alex: thx all :thumbsup:
